ITEM.PTXT: On 2WD models, a semiconductor type speed sensor & magnetic rotor integrated with the bearing unit is provided in the axle hub, with the magnetic rotor mounted to the inner race of the bearing unit and the sensor mounted on the cap side.
On 4WD models, a semiconductor type speed sensor & magnetic rotor are provided, with the magnetic rotor mounted to the inner race of the bearing unit and the sensor mounted to the rear axle.
On both 2WD and 4WD models, the operating principle of wheel speed detection is basically the same as that of the front.
The magnetic rotor consists of rubber filled with magnetic powder, with N and S poles evenly arranged in the circumferential direction (48 poles each for S and N).
When the magnetic rotor rotates, changes in the magnetic field are produced; these are detected by the active sensor and output as vehicle speed pulses.
Compared with the commonly used passive sensor, detection is possible from a vehicle speed of approximately 0km/h.
